text:
marta: Heads up — onboarding Falkor-Galaxy-13B (converted to our .rtd format) for int4 evals on Dedicated. Initial perf looks fine but we see a measurable quality regression on summarization tests compared to gemma-lite baseline. Suspect rotary/head-dim handling or vocab shadowing.

sam: Can you paste the failing prompt example and a short diff?

marta: Sure — short repro prompt: "Summarize the following conversation in 3 bullets..." outputs are verbose and inventing facts. Running batch eval with our promptset: `evals/summarize/patch_v3`.

alex: Did conversion use headwise rotary packing or per-head freq table? We had docs about Falkor having hetero-heads (some heads use 64-dim rotary, some 128).

marta: Converter used default headwise mapping (one-to-one). I attached the conversion log: `convert_falkor --map headwise --quant int4 --permute none`. ci-bot: conversion finished in 00:42, checksums OK.

lee: Could be the freq scaling. If some heads were trained with fractional rotary scaling we need to apply phase rescale during load. Try `--rotary-scale auto` and re-eval.

sam: Also check tokenizer vocab offsets — Falkor uses a shifted sentinel token for eos=50280 whereas our tokenizer expects 50256. That can cause subtle prompt truncation and hallucinations.

marta: Good call. Ran a quick smoke with `--rotary-scale auto` + corrected vocab map. Rouge and our summary metric improved ~6% but still worse than gemma baseline on factuality.

alex: How about KV cache alignment? If tokenid remap changed positions, kvcache key/vals could be misaligned and degrade context handling. Any diffs in attention layout?

marta: We compared the attention output on a small seed input between original Falkor FP32 and our int4 loader. Per-head cosine similarity drops on half the heads (0.87 -> 0.62). The pattern matches rotated-phase leakage in heads with mixed rotary dims.

lee: Two experiments I'd run in parallel: (1) force rotary per-head reindexing to original head dims (no packing), (2) load int8 fallback on the problematic heads and re-run the factuality eval. If headwise packing is the culprit, (1) should fix similarity.

sam: Also try toggling `kvcache-token-id-offset` (we had a +2 bug earlier) — cheap test, sometimes explains long-range errors.

marta: Kicking off both experiments now. I'll post short logs. If neither fixes, next step is a per-head profiling dump and we might need a small adapter to emulate original rotary phases at runtime.

ci-bot: Build queued: inference-runtime PR #4823 (marta/falkor-rotary-fix).

alex: Thanks — if you hit a perf regression from disabling packing, let us know — we can try selective remapping of only the top-K heads to preserve latency. :thumbsup:

marta: Will update within the hour with results from the two runs.
